title: GO Command Center Request V1
description: Human intent submitted as an untrusted proposal through the GitHub control bus. A Request never carries execution parameters and never holds Execution Authority. Command Center resolves every sensitive value deterministically.

request_id.description: Fresh and unique per Request. Reuse is rejected.

action_id.description: The only actions a human may name. CANARY became one in the channel revision that added it and needs no plan and no switch, because it mutates no business runtime. ROLLBACK became one in the revision that connected the proven rollback chain to the channel: like DEPLOY it mutates the eight services and takes an authenticated Request, and like the canary it needs no plan, because the deployment it undoes is derived from the Bridge's own ledger rather than named here.

x-go-capability-vs-enablement.note: A Request schema describes what is structurally expressible. It is NOT a statement of what the channel currently accepts. ChatGPT must use currently_enabled_request_action only.
x-go-capability-vs-enablement.deploy_note: The DEPLOY request capability exists in the repository and was installed by its closeout, but request enablement is fail-closed. Do not submit, imply or plan a DEPLOY Request. The live Command Center channel switch is a live-host fact that a derived control-state document must not assert.

x-go-notes: pr_number is a target selector, not an execution parameter: Command Center resolves it once to an immutable commit SHA with its own read-only resolver key.
plan_id refers to an operator-registered, human-approved deployment plan read from a fixed root-owned store. The Request cannot supply any value inside that plan. It is NOT an enabled action today.
A Request PR must add exactly one requests/<request_id>.json file and nothing else.

A CANARY Request names no image, no package and no expected-current image: those come from the root-owned canary authority file that the operator writes. Two canary Requests against the same authority differ only in identity and timing.

A ROLLBACK Request names no deployment, no service, no image and no target either. The Command Center derives the deployment to undo from the Bridge's own published ledger -- the newest successful one it signed -- and derives the images to restore from that deployment's own record on the host. Two rollback Requests would therefore ask for the same undo; the second is refused once the first has been published.
A Request never creates, signs, publishes or executes anything. Command Center is the only component that can turn a validated Request into a Signed Task.
